Title: FAO LSJ - ToGP debt repayment, NRA and Mask 1K faces

Messages.Author: legb...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
i was actually meant to be a judge in the Watford tourney [one of many]
and two things came up that i didn't really know the answer to.

1. ToGP says you MUST repay one towards your debt at the end of your
turn. Can you CHOOSE to repay any larger part, including your entire
debt, at any other time, eg during your turn so's to take your pool down
to the necessary level for calling a Parity Shift?

2. Fairly sure i am right about this next one but let's check. Vampire
A tries to bleed and is blocked. Vampire B does Mask 1K faces. i think
vampire A now can't attempt to bleed again, by NRA. Is this right? i
ruled that that was the way it worked and it lost the game for the guy
against whom i ruled it.

Sent via Deja.com http://www.deja.com/
Before you buy.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
legb...@my-deja.com wrote:
> i was actually meant to be a judge in the Watford tourney [one of
> many] and two things came up that i didn't really know the answer to.
>
> 1. ToGP says you MUST repay one towards your debt at the end of
> your turn. Can you CHOOSE to repay any larger part, including your
> entire debt, at any other time, eg during your turn so's to take
> your pool down to the necessary level for calling a Parity Shift?

No. You must repay one, and no mechanism is given for repaying more.

> 2. Fairly sure i am right about this next one but let's check.
> Vampire A tries to bleed and is blocked. Vampire B does Mask1K
> faces. i think vampire A now can't attempt to bleed again, by NRA.
> Is this right? i ruled that that was the way it worked and it
> lost the game for the guy against whom i ruled it.

No. NRA only prohibits the minion who is acting when the action
resolves from attempting the action again.

Messages.Author: hamd...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
In much the same way, these ruling were asked of me at Watford. I think
I made the right choice - what do you think...

1) A Charnas the Imp was played on a vampire. The damage he does is
said to be done at the untap phase. Can the vampire elect not to untap
and take no damage?

2) The card text says the vampire takes a damage, but it is not
aggravated. Does this mean the worst it does is torporises the vampire?
It mentions "burning". Can Charnas burn the vampire all by himself?

Cheers

DH



Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
hamd...@my-deja.com wrote:
>
> In much the same way, these ruling were asked of me at Watford. I think
> I made the right choice - what do you think...

I think your subject line needs changing... :-)

> 1) A Charnas the Imp was played on a vampire. The damage he does is
> said to be done at the untap phase. Can the vampire elect not to untap
> and take no damage?

Charnas says nothing about the untap phase, nor about allowing the
victim to elect not to untap in the untap phase.

The victim will untap in the untap phase [4].
The victim will take one damage every time he untaps, regardless of
the phase. (card text).

> 2) The card text says the vampire takes a damage, but it is not
> aggravated. Does this mean the worst it does is torporises the vampire?

Yes (or burns the ally).

> It mentions "burning". Can Charnas burn the vampire all by himself?

If the vampire is particulary strange (e.g., Julius).

--
